ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The legend on the right side of the figure indicates that a hollow square represents M, and a shaded/dotted filled circle represents X. In the cubic unit cell, the X spheres appear in ccp fashion at the 8 vertices and 6 face-center positions of the unit cell; the M squares are visible as one body-center position inside the unit cell, and another four on the edges of the unit cell. Reasoning: The count of X in ccp is: the 8 vertex X each contribute 1/8, plus the 6 face-center X each contribute 1/2, so the number of X = 8×1/8 + 6×1/2 = 1 + 3 = 4. The count of M is: 1 at the body center completely belongs to this unit cell, and 4 M on the edges each contribute 1/4, so the number of M = 1 + 4×1/4 = 2. Therefore, the composition ratio within the unit cell is M:X = 2:4, simplified to 1:2, and the empirical formula is MX_2.

method.method_draft: First describe the image: shaded circles are X and open squares are M. Count X as the ccp lattice atoms: 8 corner X atoms and 6 face-centred X atoms contribute 8×1/8 + 6×1/2 = 4 X per unit cell. Then count the M squares visible in the unit cell: one is fully inside at the body centre, and four are on edges, contributing 1 + 4×1/4 = 2 M. Reduce M2X4 to MX2.

method.method_draft: First describe the image: X is represented by shaded circles forming the ccp framework, and M is represented by open squares placed in selected interstitial positions. Use the standard ccp fact that the fcc cell of X contains 4 X atoms and has 4 octahedral voids per unit cell. From the drawing, M occupies only half of the octahedral voids indicated by the square positions, so M atoms per unit cell = 2. Therefore the composition is M2X4, which reduces to MX2.
method.CoT_raw:
Image description: The diagram shows a cubic unit cell in which shaded circles represent X atoms arranged in a ccp/fcc framework. Open squares represent M atoms placed in selected interstitial positions. The open squares are not shown at every octahedral void position; they indicate occupation of only half of the octahedral sites.
Reasoning: In a ccp arrangement, X forms an fcc unit cell, which contains 4 X atoms per unit cell. A ccp/fcc unit cell has 4 octahedral voids per unit cell. Since M occupies half of these octahedral voids, the number of M atoms per unit cell is 4 × 1/2 = 2. Thus the unit-cell composition is M2X4. Reducing the ratio 2:4 gives the empirical formula MX2.
